text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation Prime Minister, Edhem Bicakcic, calls for dismissal of Finance Minister Drago Bilandzija who he accused of allowing company from Siroki Brijeg to avoid custom taxes worth 175 million German marks ($110 million dollars).
- Bosnia's chairman of the collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, left the hospital on Tuesday after entering last week for a scheduled check-up.
- Bosnia's Council of Ministers formed four working groups which will continue to work on package of economic laws at its second session in Sarajevo suburb of Lukavica next week.

- Bosnia's biggest power company Elektroprivreda and Norwegian Power Group signed a 1.7 million German mark ($1 million) project to repair power system in the north of Bosnia. Funds and equipment has been provided by Norwegian government.
- Haris Silajdzic, co-chairman of Bosnia's cabinet, discusses creation of Saudi-Bosnian investment company with Saudi businessman and director of Sarajevo company Unis Holding.
- The electrical supply for the iron company "Zeljezara" from Zenica was cut off due to a 4 million German mark ($2.5 million) debt.
- President of Moslem-Croat Federation Kresimir Zubak met U.S. special envoy to Balkans James Pardew to discuss further development of newly created Federation army.
- Bosnia's Federation House of Representatives is due to meet to discuss draft privatisation law, restitution of nationalised property, sale of public flats, health care and insurance.

- Rory O'Sullivan, head of the World Bank mission to Bosnia, says that proposal allowing Bosnia's soldiers to convert 6 billion German Marks ($3.7 billion) worth of bank books into cash would be a mistake.
